21. Case study: glucose trajectories

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-21-case-glucose.Rmd
book-21-case-glucose.Rmd

What you will learn

Describe first and later glucose readings, distinguish change from slope, handle unobserved threshold attainment, and interpret a model with only ten people.

You need: the Opal login from Getting started and the lab lesson. This chapter uses omop.synthea.

Research question

Among people with blood-glucose measurements, how do values change over recorded follow-up? This is a lab-defined population, not a diagnosis-confirmed diabetes cohort. The Synthea data are synthetic; the cutoffs below are teaching rules.

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.synthea", server = "site")$conns

Choose a populated measurement 

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Glucose", domain = "Measurement", vocabulary = "LOINC", datasources = conns)$pooled
hits[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept")]
concept_id concept_name standard_concept
3000483 Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood S
3004501 Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma S
3009261 Glucose [Presence] in Urine by Test strip S
3024629 Glucose [Mass/volume] in Urine by Test strip S 
glucose_id <- hits$concept_id[trimws(hits$concept_name) == "Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood"]
ds.omop.concept.locate(glucose_id, type = "both", datasources = conns)$pooled
concept_id table_name concept_column n_records n_persons
3000483 measurement measurement_concept_id 225 10 
ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = glucose_id,
  type = "both", datasources = conns)$pooled[c("value", "concept_name", "n")]
value concept_name n
8840 milligram per deciliter 225 
glucose_set <- omop_concept_set(glucose_id)
saveRDS(glucose_set, "glucose-concept.rds")

Blood glucose is 3000483, recorded in 8840, milligram per deciliter (mg/dL). The locator shows a band of 225–229 rows and 10–14 people. The separate Serum or Plasma concept has records from only one person in the public synthetic source; its occurrence cannot support a released analysis. Do not combine specimens merely to increase the sample.

Select a baseline and a genuine later value

Index on first glucose. The last-value window starts the following day, so a person with only a baseline reading cannot supply a follow-up outcome. A slope uses all readings and their actual spacing; last minus first ignores how long the change took.

glucose <- omop_event("measurement", glucose_set, unit = omop_unit(8840L))
first <- omop_variable(event = glucose, reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", window = omop_window(0, 0)))
last <- omop_variable(event = glucose, reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", window = omop_window(1, NULL)))
cohort <- omop_population("measured", index = omop_index(glucose))
trajectory <- omop_recipe(populations = list(cohort), variables = list(
  first = first, last = last,
  control = omop_number_bins(last, breaks = c(-Inf, 90, Inf), labels = c("below 90", "90 or above")),
  change = omop_number_change(glucose),
  per_year = omop_number(omop_number_change(glucose, "slope", time_unit = "days"),
    omop_number_spec(transform = omop_number_transform("affine", factor = 365.25))),
  followup_days = omop_variable(event = glucose, reducer = omop_reduce("last_date", window = omop_window(1, NULL))),
  target_days = omop_number_change(glucose, "time_to_threshold", threshold = 95, op = "ge")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "measured", format = "wide"))
recipe_execute(trajectory, out = c(people = "D_glucose"), datasources = conns)
sapply(c("first", "last", "change", "per_year", "followup_days"), function(column)
  dsBaseClient::ds.quantileMean(paste0("D_glucose$", column), datasources = conns))
first last change per_year followup_days
5% 68.320 67.575 -25.715 -0.882 3357.55
10% 69.940 69.150 -23.330 -0.722 4860.10
25% 78.275 73.350 -15.275 -0.014 5423.25
50% 84.550 92.200 9.050 0.221 6562.50
75% 90.050 95.225 18.900 0.575 6872.50
90% 92.980 98.660 23.130 1.996 7008.50
95% 96.040 99.380 25.965 2.077 7028.75
Mean 83.400 85.980 2.580 0.397 5915.20

All ten people have later values, with median follow-up about 18 years. First and last means are 83.40 and 85.98 mg/dL; mean change is 2.58 mg/dL. Mean slope is 0.397 mg/dL per year (median 0.221). A change over many years is not a short-term treatment response, and a straight-line slope can miss fluctuations between readings.

Classify values and distinguish unobserved attainment 

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_glucose$control",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_glucose$control
#>    below_90 90_or_above          NA 
#>           4           6           0

Four people are below 90 and six are at least 90 mg/dL. It is a presentation rule, not a diagnosis or treatment goal. More detailed categories may be withheld in a population this small.

For a separate timing question, use the first observed glucose ≥95 mg/dL. In this tiny synthetic dataset, a 100 mg/dL rule would leave too few people for a released summary, so the lesson uses 95 mg/dL as a teaching threshold. In a real study the threshold comes from the protocol, and a withheld result is reported as withheld, not avoided by changing the cutoff.

dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_glucose$target_days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>     5%    10%    25%    50%    75%    90%    95%   Mean 
#>  259.7  519.4  986.5 1169.0 2693.5 4769.8 5555.9 2101.5
dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_glucose$target_days", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] 2

Eight people have an observed attainment and two are missing. The median among attainments is 1,169 days; the mean is 2,101.5 days. One of the eight attains at day zero, which is not shown directly by these interpolated quantiles. A zero means the threshold was met at baseline; a positive time means a later recorded crossing. Missing means no crossing was observed during available measurements. The missing people must remain under observation until censoring in a time-to-event analysis; a mean among observed crossings alone is conditional on crossing and does not estimate everyone’s time to threshold.

Model last against first with appropriate uncertainty

A Gaussian regression describes the association between first and last readings. With ten complete people and two coefficients, use a t interval with eight residual degrees of freedom rather than the large-sample z interval.

fit <- dsBaseClient::ds.glm("last ~ first", data = "D_glucose", family = "gaussian", datasources = conns)
b <- fit$coefficients["first", "Estimate"]
se <- fit$coefficients["first", "Std. Error"]
data.frame(N = fit$Nvalid, df = fit$df, Estimate = b, Lower_95 = b - qt(.975, fit$df) * se,
  Upper_95 = b + qt(.975, fit$df) * se, P_t = 2 * pt(-abs(b / se), df = fit$df))
N df Estimate Lower_95 Upper_95 P_t
10 8 -0.748 -1.616 0.119 0.082

The coefficient is about −0.75: a 1 mg/dL higher first value is associated with about 0.75 mg/dL lower last value. The t-based interval includes zero: the 95% interval is −1.616 to 0.119 and the t-based p-value is 0.082. Regression to the mean, unequal follow-up and the sample of only ten people make this association fragile; it is not evidence that high baseline glucose causes improvement.

Exercises

1. Change the time unit. Express the observed threshold times in years and retain the number with missing attainment.

Solution 1

ds.omop.mutate("D_glucose", target_years = target_days / 365.25,
  newobj = "D_glucose_years", datasources = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_glucose_years$target_years", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>         5%        10%        25%        50%        75%        90%        95%       Mean 
#>  0.7110198  1.4220397  2.7008898  3.2005476  7.3744011 13.0590007 15.2112252  5.7535934
dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_glucose_years$target_years", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] 2

The median becomes 3.20 years and the mean 5.75 years. Divide the day summary by 365.25 to check the values. The valid and missing counts do not change: rescaling cannot supply unobserved crossings.

2. Separate endpoints from a trajectory. Calculate last minus first on the server and compare with the native change summary. Does agreement prove a steady increase?

Solution 2

ds.omop.mutate("D_glucose", difference = last - first,
  newobj = "D_difference", datasources = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_difference$difference", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#> 
#> $site$length
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>      5%     10%     25%     50%     75%     90%     95%    Mean 
#> -25.715 -23.330 -15.275   9.050  18.900  23.130  25.965   2.580

The difference agrees with native change because both calculate last minus first. All ten people have later readings, so the complete-case populations also coincide. It describes only two endpoints; intermediate values can rise and fall. The slope uses those intermediate observations but still assumes a straight line.

Recap

Retain real follow-up, state the time scale, and distinguish observed crossings from censoring. Small datasets can support a useful descriptive analysis without supporting a precise or clinically predictive model.
